skill.name: csctf
skill.description: Convert shared AI conversation links into clean Markdown and static HTML transcripts with preserved code blocks and stable filenames.
skill.summary: Archive shared ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, and Claude conversations as Markdown and static HTML.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline examples, and documented file paths. The confirmed issues are remote installer commands that pipe downloads into bash, plus semantic risks around browser-session handling, automation evasion, and public transcript publishing.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash examples with download, checksum verification, local inspection, and a separate install command.
Require explicit consent before accessing browser profiles, document copied data, delete temporary profiles, and avoid handling cookies when possible.
Remove stealth and Cloudflare-bypass behavior, or clearly restrict automation to provider-approved and user-authorized workflows.
Default to dry runs, warn about public exposure, and avoid recommending confirmation bypass for publishing workflows.

content.value_statement: Shared AI conversations are hard to archive with clean formatting and stable file names. This skill documents a CLI workflow that converts supported share links into Markdown and static HTML transcripts.
actual_capabilities: Converts supported AI share links into Markdown transcripts.
Generates static HTML copies with inline styling and no JavaScript.
Preserves fenced code blocks and language hints when available.
Creates deterministic filenames with collision suffixes.
Supports optional GitHub Pages publishing through the GitHub CLI.
Handles Claude shares through a local Chrome session when logged in.
limitations: Requires public share links, except Claude shares use an active local Chrome session.
Provider layout changes can break extraction until selectors are updated.
First use may download a large Playwright Chromium browser bundle.
Publishing features require authenticated GitHub CLI access and privacy review.

use_cases.title: Archive Research Chats
use_cases.description: Save public AI research conversations as readable Markdown and HTML records for later review.

use_cases.title: Publish Team Knowledge
use_cases.description: Convert useful shared chats into static pages that a team can host and reference.

use_cases.title: Preserve Code Discussions
use_cases.description: Keep coding conversations with fenced code blocks, language labels, and stable filenames.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Share Link
prompt_templates.prompt: Use csctf to convert this public AI share link into Markdown and HTML. Keep the default filename and explain where the files are saved.

prompt_templates.title: Create Markdown Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Export this supported share link as Markdown only. Preserve code fences and avoid creating an HTML copy.

prompt_templates.title: Set Output Location
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this share link and place the output in my chosen archive folder. Use a stable name based on the conversation title.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Pages Publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a dry run for publishing selected transcript exports to GitHub Pages. Show the target repository, branch, directory, and privacy risks before publishing.

output_examples.input: A public ChatGPT share link for a debugging conversation.
output_examples.output: A Markdown transcript and a static HTML page named from the conversation title, with code sections preserved.

output_examples.input: A Claude share link opened from a browser session where the user is already logged in.
output_examples.output: A local transcript export that uses the active browser session to access the shared conversation.

output_examples.input: A set of approved transcript files prepared for publishing.
output_examples.output: A GitHub Pages-ready archive with updated index files and a viewer URL after confirmation.

best_practices: Review each transcript for secrets before conversion or publishing.
Use dry-run mode before publishing exports to GitHub Pages.
Run browser-session features only on trusted machines.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installer scripts into a shell without review.
Do not publish private or sensitive conversations to public pages.
Do not skip confirmation when repository or directory settings are unclear.

faq.question: What providers does this skill describe?
faq.answer: It covers ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, and Claude shared conversation links.

faq.question: Does it create both Markdown and HTML?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented CLI can create Markdown and static HTML outputs unless options disable one format.

faq.question: Does Claude export require a login?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude shares use a local Chrome session where the user is already logged in.

faq.question: Can it publish exports online?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents optional GitHub Pages publishing through the GitHub CLI.

faq.question: Is the generated HTML dynamic?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes static HTML output with inline styling and no JavaScript.

faq.question: What should users check before publishing?
faq.answer: Users should remove secrets, private data, access tokens, and sensitive business information from transcripts.
